claims.explanation: Atorvastatin's selective killing likely reflects dependence on the mevalonate/cholesterol synthesis pathway, which is required for geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate-mediated prenylation of small GTPases such as RAS and RHO. Lines with activating RAS/MAPK pathway mutations (NRAS, KRAS, BRAF, NF1 loss) or PTEN/PIK3CA-driven PI3K-AKT signaling appear enriched among sensitive lines, consistent with reliance on prenylated RAS/ Rho GTPases for survival, while EGFR-mutant or otherwise MAPK-independent lines are relatively protected. The virtual cell's HMGCR induction and strong transcriptional similarity to other statins supports on-target HMGCR inhibition as the mechanism.

features.basis: Activating NRAS mutations in sensitive melanoma/bladder lines; RAS requires geranylgeranylation for membrane localization and statins deplete GGPP
KRAS-mutant lines (SNU410, CL11, SNU1214) among sensitive; KRAS prenylation dependence on mevalonate pathway
BRAF-mutant melanomas (K029AX, LOXIMVI, UACC62, IPC298) enriched in sensitive set; MAPK-driven lines may depend on prenylated RAS/RHO
NF1 loss (LOXIMVI, S117, KALS1) activates RAS-MAPK and may increase dependence on prenylation
PTEN-mutant lines (FTC133, UACC62, KALS1, HEC265) among sensitive; PI3K-AKT activation may increase mevalonate pathway demand
PIK3CA-mutant lines (SNU840, HGC27) among sensitive; PI3K signaling can upregulate SREBP/HMGCR
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (NCIH1650, NCIH1648, HCC4006) are among least affected, suggesting EGFR-driven survival is less statin-dependent
Virtual cell shows HMGCR upregulation by atorvastatin, indicating on-target feedback; high baseline HMGCR expression may predict greater dependence
TP53 mutation is nearly universal across both sensitive and resistant lines, so it is not selective; listed only to note lack of discriminating value
ARID1A mutations appear in several sensitive lines (LOXIMVI, KU1919, HEC265); chromatin remodeling loss may alter sterol pathway regulation
KEAP1/NFE2L2 mutations in HEC265 sensitive line; NRF2 activation may increase metabolic demand and statin sensitivity
SF3B1 mutations in sensitive lines UO31 and HCC95; splicing factor mutations may alter HMGCR splicing or cholesterol metabolism
